A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 18-page IPA paper, including Appendices A and B. Complete text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original LoRA-asymmetry experiments, commonsense reasoning and VTAB-1k evaluations, and ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes, including the benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.4 retain the same reconstruction objective, linear projector, IPCA pretraining procedure, and optional projector fine-tuning.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 27 BBH tasks, commonsense-170k training data and eight reasoning benchmarks, and 19 VTAB-1k classification tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–4 and 6–7, including LoRA, DoRA, PiSSA, OLoRA, CorDA, RandLoRA, VeRA, random orthogonal projections, and vision fine-tuning controls.

E3.justification: The model configurations, preprocessing, splits, metrics, training budgets, and ablation settings remain unchanged, including three-epoch language adaptation and the 100-epoch vision evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the same projector fine-tuning, IPCA-versus-GHA, hidden-dimension, pretraining-size, compute-budget, and feature-similarity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same two-sided paired sign tests across 19 tasks. Seed information and statistical reporting elsewhere are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain identical numerical entries. The result graphics and accompanying descriptions also match; no results, rankings, or qualitative findings are added or revised.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, LoRA gradient equations, reconstruction objective, PCA formulation, and Appendix B feature-similarity expression are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about information-preserving projection, improved adaptation accuracy, and comparable performance with roughly half the trainable parameters.

C2.justification: Interpretations of LoRA asymmetry, ablation findings, computational tradeoffs, and future research directions are identical. The added acknowledgment disclaimer introduces no scientific qualification.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, code access information, and the IDRIS/GENCI HPC allocation remain unchanged. The added EU funding credit supplies no new implementation or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the reference entries are unchanged. The relationship to prior research and novelty positioning remain identical.

P1.justification: v3 expands the acknowledgment with EU funding, Horizon Europe grant 101214398 (ELLIOT), and a responsibility disclaimer. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgment causes local reflow on pages 11–12, slightly shifting Figure 4 and changing reference spacing. Figure graphics and table structures remain identical; fifteen pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 adds EU/ELLIOT funding disclosure to the retained HPC acknowledgment, making funding attribution more complete. The scientific argument, evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices are unchanged. This administrative addition and limited layout reflow do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
